    13→// The lifecycle of the NSE looks something like the following:
    14→//  1)  App receives notification
    15→//  2)  System creates an instance of the extension class
    16→//      and calls `didReceive` in the background
    17→//  3)  Extension processes messages / displays whatever
    18→//      notifications it needs to
    19→//  4)  Extension notifies its work is complete by calling
    20→//      the contentHandler
    21→//  5)  If the extension takes too long to perform its work
    22→//      (more than 30s), it will be notified and immediately
    23→//      terminated
    24→//
    25→// Note that the NSE does *not* always spawn a new process to
    26→// handle a new notification and will also try and process notifications
    27→// in parallel. `didReceive` could be called twice for the same process,
    28→// but it will always be called on different threads. It may or may not be
    29→// called on the same instance of `NotificationService` as a previous
    30→// notification.

    33→    static let receivedWhileOfflineNotificationID = "io.element.elementx.receivedWhileOfflineNotification"
    34→    
    35→    private static var targetConfiguration: Target.ConfigurationResult?
    36→

    43→    private var notificationHandler: NotificationHandler?

    47→    private var cancellables: Set<AnyCancellable> = []

    49→    /// We can make the whole NSE a MainActor after https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolution/blob/main/proposals/0371-isolated-synchronous-deinit.md
    50→    /// otherwise we wouldn't be able to log the tag in the deinit.
    51→    deinit {
    52→        ExtensionLogger.logMemory(with: tag)
    53→        MXLog.info("\(tag) deinit")
    54→    }
    55→    
    56→    override init() {
    57→        appHooks = AppHooks()
    58→        appHooks.setUp()
    59→        
    60→        // If the device is still locked then we can't write to the app group container and
    61→        // the target configuration will fail. We could call exit(0) here, however with the
    62→        // notification filtering entitlement that results in the notification being discarded
    63→        // so we need to wait for the delegate method to be called and bail out there instead.
    64→        if !BootDetectionManager.isDeviceLockedAfterReboot(containerURL: URL.appGroupContainerDirectory),
    65→           Self.targetConfiguration == nil {
    66→            Self.targetConfiguration = Target.nse.configure(logLevel: settings.logLevel,
    67→                                                            traceLogPacks: settings.traceLogPacks,
    68→                                                            sentryURL: nil,
    69→                                                            rageshakeURL: settings.bugReportRageshakeURL,
    70→                                                            appHooks: appHooks)
    71→        }
    72→

    76→    override func didReceive(_ request: UNNotificationRequest, withContentHandler contentHandler: @escaping (UNNotificationContent) -> Void) {
    77→        Task { await handle(request, withContentHandler: contentHandler) }
    78→    }
    79→    
    80→    private func handle(_ request: UNNotificationRequest, withContentHandler contentHandler: @escaping (UNNotificationContent) -> Void) async {
    81→        // If we skipped configuring the target it means we can't write to the app group, so we're unlikely to
    82→        // be able to create a session (and even if we could, we would be missing the lightweightTokioRuntime).
    83→        // Additionally, APNs servers only store the most recent notification when the device is powered off.
    84→        // So lets a) skip processing the notification and b) deliver a special "offline" notification as a workaround.
    85→        guard Self.targetConfiguration != nil else {
    86→            // MXLog isn't configured:
    87→            // swiftlint:disable:next print_deprecation
    88→            print("Device is locked after reboot.")

    90→            if Self.hasHandledFirstNotificationSinceBoot {
    91→                return contentHandler(request.content)

    98→        
    99→        guard !shouldDeliverReceivedWhileOfflineNotification() else {

   104→            return contentHandler(.init())

   107→        guard let roomID = request.content.roomID else {
   108→            // Don't log until the app hooks have been run:
   109→            // swiftlint:disable:next print_deprecation
   110→            print("Missing roomID, bailing out.")
   111→            return contentHandler(request.content)

   158→                                                      notificationContent: mutableContent,
   159→                                                      tag: tag)

   162→            MXLog.info("\(tag) Configured user session")

   167→        }
   168→    }

   170→    override func serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire() {

   174→    // MARK: - Boot handling
   175→    
   176→    /// The APNs servers only store the most recent notification when delivery fails. So when the user first boots
   177→    /// their phone we need to use some approximations to decide whether or not the first notification may potentially
   178→    /// represent more than one message. When that appears possible we replace the notification's content with the special
   179→    /// "received while offline" notification as a more prominent prompt for to the user to open the app and check all their chats.
   180→    ///
   181→    /// Note that this only handles the first-boot case. When the SDK is able to compute the unread count, we should start to use the NSE,
   182→    /// remote-notifications (content-available) and background app refreshes to fetch and deliver our notifications as a more robust solution.
   183→    private func shouldDeliverReceivedWhileOfflineNotification() -> Bool {
   184→        if Self.hasHandledFirstNotificationSinceBoot {
   185→            // If we've already handled the first notification in this process there's no need to continue.
   186→            return false
   187→        }
   188→        
   189→        Self.hasHandledFirstNotificationSinceBoot = true
   190→        
   191→        guard let currentBootTime = BootDetectionManager.systemBootTime() else {
   192→            // There's not much we can do if the boot time is unknown, so don't show the offline notification.
   193→            return false
   194→        }
   195→        
   196→        guard let lastKnownBootTime = settings.lastNotificationBootTime else {
   197→            // Assume a missing boot time indicates a fresh installation…
   198→            // So store the current boot time but let the notification through.
   199→            settings.lastNotificationBootTime = currentBootTime
   200→            return false
   201→        }
   202→        
   203→        if abs(lastKnownBootTime - currentBootTime) < 1 {
   204→            return false
   205→        }
   206→        
   207→        // This is the first notification since boot, store the boot time.
   208→        settings.lastNotificationBootTime = currentBootTime
   209→        
   210→        // At this point it becomes a trade-off. Once the device has been powered on for a long enough amount
   211→        // of time it is a reasonable assumption that the device has now connected to a network and that any
   212→        // notification is actually new rather than having been sent whilst the device was powered off.
   213→        //
   214→        // Note: We could actually solve this by having Sygnal add a timestamp to the notification payload 🤔
   215→        if Date.now.timeIntervalSince(Date(timeIntervalSince1970: currentBootTime)) > Self.firstNotificationThreshold {
   216→            return false
   217→        } else {
   218→            return true
   219→        }
   220→    }
   221→    
   222→    /// Delivers a generic notification informing the user that they have one or more new messages.
   223→    ///
   224→    /// Note: it is safe to call this method multiple times as it simply replaces any existing instance of the notification
   225→    /// with a fresh copy, meaning it won't queue multiple copies but will still re-play the notification sound.
   226→    private func deliverReceivedWhileOfflineNotification(for originalRequest: UNNotificationRequest) {
   227→        // This is intended to be called before the app hooks have been run, so don't log:
   228→        // swiftlint:disable:next print_deprecation
   229→        print("Delivering the 'received while offline' notification.")
   230→        
   231→        let content = UNMutableNotificationContent()
   232→        content.body = L10n.notificationReceivedWhileOfflineIos
   233→        content.badge = originalRequest.content.unreadCount as NSNumber?
   234→        content.sound = .init(named: .init("message.caf"))
   235→        
   236→        let request = UNNotificationRequest(identifier: Self.receivedWhileOfflineNotificationID, content: content, trigger: nil)
   237→        UNUserNotificationCenter.current().add(request)
   238→    }

   240→    // MARK: - Logging
   241→    
   242→    private var tag: String {
   243→        "[NSE][\(Unmanaged.passUnretained(self).toOpaque())][\(Unmanaged.passUnretained(Thread.current).toOpaque())][\(ProcessInfo.processInfo.processIdentifier)]"
   244→    }
   245→}

    43→    func processEvent(_ eventID: String, roomID: String) async {

    95→        }

    97→        guard case let .timeline(event) = itemProxy.event else {
    98→            return .shouldDisplay
    99→        }

   104→            case .poll,
   105→                 .roomEncrypted,
   106→                 .sticker:

   156→    /// Handle incoming call notifications.
   157→    /// - Returns: A boolean indicating whether the notification was handled and should now be discarded.
   158→    private func handleCallNotification(notificationType: RtcNotificationType,
   159→                                        rtcNotifyEventID: String,
   160→                                        timestamp: Timestamp,
   161→                                        expirationTimestamp: Timestamp,
   162→                                        roomID: String,
   163→                                        roomDisplayName: String) async -> NotificationProcessingResult {
   164→        // Handle incoming VoIP calls, show the native OS call screen
   165→        // https://developer.apple.com/documentation/callkit/sending-end-to-end-encrypted-voip-calls
   166→        //
   167→        // The way this works is the following:
   168→        // - the NSE receives the notification and decrypts it
   169→        // - checks if it's still time relevant (max 10 seconds old) and whether it should ring
   170→        // - otherwise it goes on to show it as a normal notification
   171→        // - if it should ring then it discards the notification but invokes `reportNewIncomingVoIPPushPayload`
   172→        // so that the main app can handle it
   173→        // - the main app picks this up in `PKPushRegistry.didReceiveIncomingPushWith` and
   174→        // `CXProvider.reportNewIncomingCall` to show the system UI and handle actions on it.
   175→        // N.B. this flow works properly only when background processing capabilities are enabled
   176→        guard notificationType == .ring else {
   177→            MXLog.info("Non-ringing call notification, handling as push notification")
   178→            return .shouldDisplay
   179→        }
   180→        
   181→        // Check to see if a call is still ongoing
   182→        if let room = userSession.roomForIdentifier(roomID) { // Try to get call details from the room info
   183→            if !room.hasActiveRoomCall() { // If I don't have an active call wait a bit and make sure
   184→                let expiringTask = ExpiringTaskRunner {
   185→                    await withCheckedContinuation { [weak self] continuation in
   186→                        self?.roomInfoObservationToken = room.subscribeToRoomInfoUpdates(listener: SDKListener { info in
   187→                            if info.hasRoomCall {
   188→                                MXLog.info("Received room info update and the room has an active call now.")
   189→                                continuation.resume()
   190→                            } else {
   191→                                MXLog.info("Received a room info update but the room still doesn't have an ongoing call.")
   192→                            }
   193→                        })
   194→                    }
   195→                }
   196→                
   197→                try? await expiringTask.run(timeout: .seconds(5)) // Wait 5 seconds or just use whatever is available
   198→                
   199→                guard room.hasActiveRoomCall() else {
   200→                    MXLog.info("The room no longer has an ongoing call, handling as push notification")
   201→                    return .shouldDisplay
   202→                }
   203→            }
   204→        } else { // Otherwise fallback to the old timeout mechanism
   205→            let timestamp = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: TimeInterval(timestamp / 1000))
   206→            
   207→            guard abs(timestamp.timeIntervalSinceNow) < ElementCallServiceNotificationDiscardDelta else {
   208→                MXLog.info("Call notification is too old, handling as push notification")
   209→                return .shouldDisplay
   210→            }
   211→        }
   212→        
   213→        let expirationDate = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: TimeInterval(expirationTimestamp / 1000))
   214→        let payload = [ElementCallServiceNotificationKey.roomID.rawValue: roomID,
   215→                       ElementCallServiceNotificationKey.roomDisplayName.rawValue: roomDisplayName,
   216→                       ElementCallServiceNotificationKey.expirationDate.rawValue: expirationDate,
   217→                       ElementCallServiceNotificationKey.rtcNotifyEventID.rawValue: rtcNotifyEventID] as [String: Any]
   218→        
   219→        do {
   220→            try await CXProvider.reportNewIncomingVoIPPushPayload(payload)
   221→            MXLog.info("Call notification delegated to CallKit")
   222→        } catch {
   223→            MXLog.error("Failed reporting voip call with error: \(error). Handling as push notification")
   224→            return .shouldDisplay
   225→        }
   226→        
   227→        return .processedShouldDiscard
   228→    }
